name: San Francisco
tagline: Tech Capital, Iconic Fog, and a World-Class Food Scene by the Golden Gate
description: San Francisco is one of the most expensive cities in the United States, but for those who can afford it, the rewards are extraordinary. Perched on a hilly peninsula between the Pacific Ocean and the San Francisco Bay, the city offers a Mediterranean climate, a Michelin-starred food scene rivaling any in the world, and a cultural energy fueled by decades of innovation. FIRE retirees face steep housing costs and California's high state income tax, but gain access to stunning natural beauty, world-class healthcare at UCSF, and a walkable urban core unlike anything else on the West Coast.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate – property crime is high, violent crime varies by neighborhood
quickFacts.climate: Mediterranean with cool, foggy summers and mild, wet winters

housing.description: A modest studio in an outer neighborhood like the Sunset or Richmond, where the city's high rental floor sets the largest line

dining.description: Occasional, inexpensive dining — Mission burritos, Richmond dim sum, street food — with most meals cooked at home

healthcare.description: Covered California (Region 4) individual Silver, subsidized under the cliff; Bay Area premiums hold a high floor. Assumes an early retiree (45–55); older retirees budget more.

transportation.description: Car-free on a Muni monthly pass; Muni plus BART covers the dense, walkable city

entertainment.description: The free city — the Presidio, Lands End, Golden Gate Park, and the bridge

1M.lifestyle: San Francisco at its most disciplined, but genuinely livable. Housing is a modest studio in an outer neighborhood like the Sunset or Richmond — the city's high rental floor means this is the single largest line by far, and it does not compress. The upside is a car-free life: a Muni pass plus BART covers the dense, walkable city. Dining out is occasional and inexpensive — Mission burritos, Richmond dim sum, street food — with most meals cooked at home. Recreation is the free city: the Presidio, Lands End, Golden Gate Park, and the bridge itself. Housing and healthcare alone dominate the budget, but the setting is extraordinary.

dining.description: Dining out regularly at the city's celebrated mid-range restaurants

healthcare.description: An unsubsidized individual plan at or just above the cliff, Bay Area Silver/Gold for the age band

3M.lifestyle: A comfortable city life in a quality one-bedroom in a desirable central neighborhood like Hayes Valley, Nob Hill, or Russian Hill. Dining out regularly at the city's celebrated mid-range restaurants, weekend drives to Napa and Sonoma, and memberships at SFMOMA or the symphony all fit without constant budget math. Still largely car-free on Muni and BART, with rideshare filling the gaps. A comprehensive private health plan and world-class care at UCSF round out one of the most culturally rich urban lives on the West Coast.

10M.lifestyle: The top of San Francisco living, anchored by a luxury 2-bedroom penthouse in a prime building in Pacific Heights, the Marina, or on the waterfront, with bay or ocean views. A private chef, Michelin-level dining, a luxury car with garage parking and car service, full household staff, and UCSF concierge medicine are simply routine, alongside first-class international travel and patron-level involvement in the city's arts institutions. Even after California's top tax bite, the budget supports a genuinely wealthy life anchored by Northern California's food, wine, and natural beauty.
